title: JSON Schema
subtitle: Validate JSON contracts and apply declared defaults
intro: Check JSON documents against a schema inside SQL, report exactly what failed, and fill missing properties from schema defaults. Drafts 4 through 2020-12 are selected by $schema; a schema without one uses 2020-12.

reference.name: json_schema_is_valid(schema, data)
reference.description: Return TRUE or FALSE; invalid data never raises an error.

reference.name: json_schema_errors(schema, data)
reference.description: List path, keyword and message per failure; [] when valid.

reference.name: json_schema_validate(schema, data)
reference.description: Return TRUE, or raise an error naming up to five failures.

reference.name: json_schema_validate_schema(schema)
reference.description: Check that the schema itself is accepted before relying on it.

reference.name: json_schema_patch(schema, data)
reference.description: Return JSON Patch operations for missing defaults.

reference.name: json_schema_update(schema, data)
reference.description: Return the document with defaults applied.

reference.name: "$schema": "…/draft-07/schema#"
reference.description: Choose draft 4, 6, 7, 2019-09 or 2020-12; unknown values are errors.

notes.title: Make validation policy explicit
notes.body: Filter with json_schema_is_valid and report with json_schema_errors; use json_schema_validate where nonconforming input should abort the query. Lint the schema first, so a bad contract cannot quietly mark every row invalid.

notes.title: Drafts, formats and patterns
notes.body: Declare draft-07 for array-form tuple items. format is validated, and pattern uses RE2, so lookaround and backreferences are schema errors. Remote $ref targets are not loaded. Defaults apply only through patch and update.

examples.title: Flag valid and invalid rows
examples.caption: No TRY wrapper is needed: a violating row returns false.

examples.title: Explain each failure
examples.caption: One row per failing keyword, located by JSON Pointer.

examples.title: Fill a missing property
examples.caption: The patch contains an add operation at /retries with value 3.

assertions: SELECT CASE WHEN json_schema_validate('{"type":"integer"}', '5') AND NOT json_schema_is_valid('{"type":"integer"}', '"five"') AND (json_schema_update(getvariable('schema'), '{}')->>'retries') = '3' AND (json_schema_patch(getvariable('schema'), '{}')->>'$[0].op') = 'add' THEN true ELSE error('JSON Schema contract mismatch') END;

SELECT CASE WHEN json_schema_errors('{"properties":{"age":{"minimum":0}}}', '{"age":-1}')[1].path = '/age' AND json_schema_errors('{"properties":{"age":{"minimum":0}}}', '{"age":-1}')[1].keyword = 'minimum' AND len(json_schema_errors('{"type":"integer"}', '5')) = 0 THEN true ELSE error('json_schema_errors mismatch') END;

SELECT CASE WHEN NOT json_schema_is_valid('{"$schema":"https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema","prefixItems":[{"type":"integer"}]}', '["x"]') THEN true ELSE error('2020-12 prefixItems not enforced') END;
